assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Restoring str(row.get("plan") or "") in section_holds._row_parts leaves the held map empty and the recorded negative control reddens exactly so (AssertionError: ... did not read as landed to the section-hold read: []).
Reverting snapshot._candidates_scan to row.get("plan") leaves the node-id match with no plan match, so counted stays empty and both assertions redden.
Reverting outcomes.summarize to r.get("plan") stops the hold matching the brief-carried row, so later_run_id reads None where LANDED is asserted.
Reverting replay to str(record.get("plan") or "") makes the rebuilt request name no plan, so by_node["brief-landed"] reads empty instead of NAMED.
Reverting schedule.derive_schedule to run.get("plan") leaves runs_by_slug empty, the plan's bar is never bucketed, and the held-state assertion reddens.
Reverting capabilities to the flat field drops the observation (empty plan has no estimate) and leaves later_paths empty so reworked counts 0 instead of 1.
A resolver that answers a wildcard plan attributes the unplanned run to a named plan and the not-claimed assertion reddens.

findings.text: _lane_advisory_costs reads a ledger row's plan from the flat field (run.get("plan"), again at :571) over rows returned by ledger.load, so a run dispatched with a brief is invisible to the lane advisory; the brief required every further such reader to be repaired or named under outside_scope, and this one is in neither, so the goal's "every reader outside the ledger" is not reached.

the diff moves pick's inline attempt tally onto row_plan but no added case exercises pick: tests/test_a_brief_carried_run_counts_toward_its_section.py:201 covers snapshot._candidates_scan only, so restoring row.get("plan") at this line would leave the gate green.

the after_suite command is truncated mid-path ("...test_a_brief_carried_run_keeps"), so the head gate cannot be re-run from the record, and the arms are not the same command over the same files: base2-1318819.log runs 58 tests while head3-1318826.log runs 71, the difference being the new file plus the four cases of tests/test_a_brief_carried_run_keeps_its_plan.py the base arm omits.

the base-revision reproduction ends with a bare "EXIT" line followed by "EXIT=0" although its body records 8 failed, 1 passed, and neither this log nor head3-1318826.log carries a header naming the revision and command, so a reader taking the capture line as the status reads a red demonstration as green.
